subject: Horizon — proposed indemnity redlines and evidence/insurance ask
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@horizonhealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft Order Form redlines — indemnity

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo and the follow-up materials. Attached you'll find Horizon's redline to the Order Form with an annotated note on indemnity. High level asks from our side: 

- Cap Redwood's indemnity for third-party IP claims at $1,000,000 per claim / aggregate.
- Exclude open-source claims and claims arising solely from customer-supplied content.
- If defense costs are claimed, we need either an insurer endorsement naming Horizon or proof of insurance that covers IP defense costs.
- Evidence package required with any claim: complaint, alleged infringing prompt/output, logs showing usage, and any customer-provided materials.

We understand this is a negotiation — we're open to a defend-and-reimburse construct where Redwood can take control of defense but Horizon can step in if a conflict arises, and an escrow or insurer-backed remediation fund if endorsement is not available.

Can you run this by legal and send proposed language? Also suggest times for a 30-minute legal-to-legal call with our counsel this week. Thu 8/21 10:30am PT would work for us.

Attachments: Horizon_Redlines_20250820.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Elena Morales

On Wed, Aug 20, 2025 at 9:12 AM Elena Morales <elena.morales@horizonhealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo and the follow-up materials. Attached you'll find Horizon's redline...

Team / Elena — attached is an initial Redwood-proposed redline for the indemnity block (file: Redwood_Proposed_Indemnity_Language_v1.docx). Key points in our proposal: 

1) Defense v Reimburse: We propose "Redwood shall defend Horizon against third-party claims alleging IP infringement and shall pay costs, damages, and settlements up to the capped amount" with a carve allowing Horizon to assume defense if Redwood has a conflict of interest. That gives Horizon control if necessary but preserves Redwood's right to manage defense.

2) Cap structure: We can accept a cap of $1,000,000 per claim and $1,000,000 aggregate for claims arising solely from Redwood model outputs, subject to exceptions for willful misconduct. We push back on an uncapped customer-supplied content scenario.

3) OSS/external dependencies: We add explicit language excluding third-party open source components and upstream data provenance claims from Redwood indemnity scope.

4) Insurance/escrow alternative: If Redwood's carrier cannot issue the requested endorsement, we propose: (i) an escrow fund seeded at execution equal to X% of estimated exposure (placeholder to discuss), or (ii) a covenant from Redwood to maintain IP defense insurance and to provide a certificate of insurance annually.

5) Evidence & timing: Drafted a detailed notice and evidence checklist (see section 4.2 of the docx) —complaint, specific outputs, logs, and any customer-supplied prompts. Also included a 30-day cure notice when applicable.

Next steps: Elena, if the proposed wording is directionally acceptable, let's do the legal-to-legal call 8/21 10:30am PT. On the call we can: agree cap, OSS carveout text, and whether escrow or insurer endorsement is needed. Ben / Avery — please confirm who owns the procurement/ops follow-up for evidence collection if a claim happens.

Attachments: Redwood_Proposed_Indemnity_Language_v1.docx (docx)

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Thanks Marissa — the proposed language is helpful and closer to what Horizon can accept. A couple of points before the call: 

- We need clarity on the "conflict" carve for defense control — please add objective examples or a short arbitration path so Horizon isn't forced into open-ended disputes.
- On the escrow: can you propose a concrete initial amount (even a formula tied to ARR) so procurement can budget?
- Insurance endorsement: if Redwood can provide a COI naming Horizon and an endorsement for IP defense, that would be the preferred route. If not, we'll expect the escrow route.

We're ready to take the call tomorrow 8/26 10:30am PT if that works better for Redwood counsel. Also please confirm whether Redwood can accept an exception to liability for claims that arise solely from customer-provided training data.

Linking our procurement doc here: https://horizonhealth.sharepoint.com/sites/procurement/Redwood_RFP

Best,
Elena
